disposition_reason: ICP-MS survey of 17 elements in 54 vegetables, 36 ice creams and 31 wines from Slovenia; the main text prints selected single-sample values (maxima, minima, exceedances) and non-detect statements, while the full per-sample tables are only in the supplement.

study.design: market and home-produced food survey with health risk assessment
study.origin: Slovenian and imported vegetables (Spain, Morocco, Greece, Netherlands, Austria, Egypt), home-grown garden vegetables; local artisan and industrial ice creams; homemade and store-bought wines
study.market: grocery stores in Maribor and Slovenj Gradec; confectionery shops, kiosks and stands; gardens and wine cellars, Slovenia
study.method: microwave-assisted wet digestion (HNO3/H2O2/water); ICP-MS (Shimadzu ICPMS-2030) with internal standards
lod: LOD/LOQ per element in Table S5 (supplement, not available)
study.qa: spike recoveries 80-120%, RSD <15%; CCV every 12 injections; no food CRM

findings.reported: Pb below the LOD in W-4
findings.notes: Per-litre; LOD in Table S5 (not available).

controls.outcome: Authors state local ice creams had higher content of all elements except As, Mo and Sn; group means in Tables S15-S18 (supplement, not available)
All nine wines exceeding the OIV Pb limit (100 µg/L) were homemade; highest Pb 5603.8 µg/L (W-12), attributed to an old winepress
Home-grown vegetables qualitatively higher in Ba, Cd, Fe, Ga, Mo; store-bought higher in Al, As, Co, Cr, Cu, Mn, Ni, Sr, Zn; no group values in main text

unresolved: Full per-sample results (Tables S6-S11) and LOD/LOQ (Table S5) are in the supplementary material, not found next to the PDF; only text-printed values recorded.
IC-29 is described as vanilla-flavoured (Cr exceedance) and as chocolate-flavoured (Al, Fe) on p. 1104; flavour left unresolved.
Vegetable type of V-43 not stated in the text.
Values shown in Figures 2-4 (As, Cd, Cr, Pb per sample) not read off the charts.
Wine W-12 Cu printed 105,399.1 µg/L in text and 105,399.0 µg/L in abstract.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Limits applied (Table 2): ice cream As 0.1, Cd 0.0026, Cr 0.3, Pb 0.02 mg/kg; wine OIV As 0.2, Cd 0.01, Pb 0.10 mg/L; vegetables Cd 50, Pb 100, Cr 500 ng/g
Highest HI 4.86 green bell pepper (Morocco), 5.98 homemade red wine; ice creams no significant risk
